newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh opposition demands poll chief quit.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh opposition demands poll chief quit.

text.p: The main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party on Saturday demanded the immediate resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Abu Hena for allegedly failing to hold Thursday's parliamentary by-elections freely.

Several top party leaders, including Secretary-General Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan, told a 10,000-strong rally in Dhaka the polls were marred by fraud, intimidation, ballot-stuffing and attacks by activists from the ruling Awami League.

They called for a re-run of the election in two out of 15 constituencies contested. The Awami League of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina won eight constituencies in what local and foreign monitors said was a peaceful and fair vote.
Abu Hena also described the by-elections as "free, impartial and peaceful," which he said had demonstrated people's firm determination to uphold democracy.
The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), led by former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, also called for countrywide protests on Sunday.
Witnesses said BNP activists attacked and damaged two buses while dispersing from the rally.
Bangladesh held general elections on June 12, with the Awami League winning 146 of 300 parliamentary seats. Hasina took over as prime minister on June 23.
The BNP won 116 seats, followed by the Jatiya Party with 32.
Bangladeshi law allows candidates to run in more than one constituency, but they can retain only one seat.
The by-elections were held in districts vacated by winners who had opted for other parliamentary seats. Voting in a 16th constituency has been delayed.
The BNP and the Jatiya Party headed by jailed former president Hossain Mohammad Ershad each won three seats and an independent candidate secured one from Thursday's voting.
Awami leaders rejected BNP's allegations as baseless and hollow, saying they are trying to make an issue out of nothing.
